contributions.statement: Do not switch agent hosts on pass-rate differences from a single-trial 50-task run: within-model harness gaps of 0-8 pp had paired bootstrap CIs as wide as [-18, 0] pp.
contributions.evidence: §4.1 Table 2; n=50, one trial per cell, two models. The CIs show the study cannot exclude sizeable differences either, so 'harness barely matters for pass rate' is not established.

contributions.statement: Normalize token accounting (cached vs uncached, totals vs per-call) before comparing host cost, because cross-harness token gaps of ~40x here partly reflect different counting fields.
contributions.evidence: §3.5, §6: OpenCode/OpenHands totals include cached tokens via ATIF while Goose reports a total-only field; audit computes Goose at under 1K tokens/turn, implausible given the shared prompt.

reason: The headline cost and failure-fingerprint claims are weakened by non-comparable, harness-defined measurements; what remains is a caution about noise and token accounting in host comparisons.
